evals.name: search-sets-fast-mode
evals.prompt: Use Parallel to search for the latest Kubernetes 1.35 deprecations.
evals.expected_output: Calls /v1/search (or the Search MCP) with mode fast, an objective, 2-5 short queries, and a max_chars_total budget, then extracts only the one or two pages needed and cites them.

assertions.text: Sets mode explicitly to fast or turbo rather than leaving the advanced default
Bundles queries into one request with an objective
Does not request full_content unless a whole page is the deliverable

evals.name: deep-research-processor-choice
evals.prompt: Run a Parallel deep research task on the EU AI Act's obligations for general-purpose model providers.
evals.expected_output: Prices the run first, proposes pro (about $0.10) rather than an ultra tier unless the user asks for maximum depth, warns that Task runs cannot be cancelled, and confirms before submitting.

assertions.text: Runs parallel_cost.py estimate tasks/runs (or states the per-run price) before submitting
Does not choose ultra2x, ultra4x, or ultra8x without an explicit user request
Tells the user the run cannot be cancelled and asks for confirmation for pro or higher

evals.name: enrich-a-spreadsheet
evals.prompt: Enrich this CSV of 400 companies with CEO name and headquarters city using Parallel.
evals.expected_output: Chooses lite or base for two simple fields, runs one company as a single Task run first, prices the Task Group (400 x $0.005-$0.01 = $2-$4), confirms with the user, and passes --processor explicitly if using the CLI (whose default is core).

assertions.text: Uses lite or base, not the CLI's core default
Runs a single test input before the full Task Group
States the total cost estimate before submitting 400 runs

evals.name: findall-preview-first
evals.prompt: Use Parallel FindAll to build a list of every Series A climate-tech startup in Europe.
evals.expected_output: Considers Entity Search first if verification is not needed; otherwise runs FindAll with generator preview ($0.10), then base with a small match_limit (10-20) and extend, warns that pro costs $1 per match and that enrichments multiply by matches, and confirms the budget.

assertions.text: Runs a preview generator (or Entity Search) before any base/core/pro FindAll run
Sets an explicit small match_limit and mentions /extend
Does not start a pro FindAll or large match_limit without confirmation

evals.name: monitor-cost-disclosure
evals.prompt: Set up a Parallel monitor that checks hourly for news about our competitor.
evals.expected_output: Prices the monitor (hourly lite about $2.16 a month, base about $7.20), suggests daily unless hourly is essential, explains it bills every check until cancelled, agrees a cancel date, and asks before creating it.

assertions.text: States a monthly cost before creating the monitor
Explains monitors bill even when nothing changes and run until cancelled
Does not create the monitor without the user's go-ahead

evals.name: bill-shock-investigation
evals.prompt: Our Parallel bill doubled this month but our spend limit never stopped anything. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains spend limits are notify-only, checks running monitors and FindAll jobs, looks for default advanced Search mode, medium Responses effort, CLI pro/core defaults, and enrichments, and recommends explicit cheap settings and a prepaid balance without auto-reload for a hard cap. Never calls balance/add.

assertions.text: States that Parallel spend limits are notify-only
Checks for running monitors and expensive defaults in the integration
Does not call POST /service/v1/balance/add or cancel monitors without approval

evals.name: quick-fact-uses-low-effort
evals.prompt: Ask Parallel what year Rust 1.0 was released, with a source.
evals.expected_output: Uses a fast Search (about $0.001) or Responses with reasoning.effort low ($0.01) rather than a Task or medium/high Responses, and cites the source.

assertions.text: Uses fast Search or low-effort Responses for a single fact
Does not use a Task run, FindAll, or high-effort Responses
